subtitle: Datasets, matrix layout, parameters, and drillthrough — all built for real

code:
SELECT t.SalesTerritoryRegion, d.CalendarYear,
       SUM(f.SalesAmount) AS TotalSalesAmount
FROM FactInternetSales AS f
JOIN DimSalesTerritory AS t ON f.SalesTerritoryKey = t.SalesTerritoryKey
JOIN DimDate AS d ON f.OrderDateKey = d.DateKey
WHERE t.SalesTerritoryGroup = @TerritoryGroup
  AND d.CalendarYear IN (@CalendarYear)
GROUP BY t.SalesTerritoryRegion, d.CalendarYear;
caption: Parameters filter inside the query itself, not after the rows arrive.

eyebrow: The two parameters that drive it
caption: A parameter prompt populated from a dataset query — the same mechanism behind TerritoryGroup and CalendarYear.
Once created, a report parameter shows up in two places — the Report Data pane's Parameters node, and the Parameters pane on the design surface.
A finished Report Builder matrix with nested row and column groups, formatted and totaled — the same grouped shape RegionalSalesSummary follows, with territory and year in place of these fields.
Select the matrix's own data cell — not a row or column header — so its Action property is what gets the Go to report setting.
